name: Check
on: [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  local-workflow:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: source/requirements.txt
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: '24'
      - name: Install FFmpeg
        timeout-minutes: 5
        run: |
          if ! command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null; then
            for mirror in /etc/apt/apt-mirrors.txt /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources; do
              if [ -f "$mirror" ]; then
                sudo sed -i 's/azure.archive.ubuntu.com/archive.ubuntu.com/g' "$mirror"
              fi
            done
            sudo apt-get update
            sudo apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=2 -o Acquire::http::Timeout=30 install -y --no-install-recommends ffmpeg
          fi
      - run: python -m pip install -r source/requirements.txt
      - run: python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
        timeout-minutes: 5
      - run: python atlas.py doctor

# Do this location

Apple Silicon macOS, everything local. `atlas.py make "LOCATION"` only prepares a registered source. Beauty and accurate colour come from your source work and review, steps 1 to 4. Each city gets a separate real map, explorer and film. Say plainly what you could not source or verify.

1. Run `./setup.sh`, then `python3 atlas.py make "LOCATION"`. Inspect the native source. Reuse bundled source PNGs for the two examples; `demo --open` needs no models. Unknown places start as an untextured OSM/terrain block model, 1024×640; widen the frame in a copied recipe for a larger map. Improve licensed imagery, geometry and real roof colours before changing prompts: find aerial, DSM or mesh data and write a `photographic` or `surface` recipe. With no such data the result stays a plain illustrative starter; report that. Fresh source-bound landmark inputs require remeasurement. [Sources](docs/sources.md).
2. Choose one recognisable landmark cluster and a literal native 1024-square crop. Set up models with `./setup.sh --models` (about 9 GB, non-commercial model terms; tell the user first). Styling runs in the isolated MFlux worker, or a compatible job queue named by `ATLAS_IMAGINE`. That worker has repainted the full Edinburgh example, 10 windows at about 2.5 minutes and 18 GB each, and painted the windows of a new Amsterdam map that an agent then finished with reviewed repairs; smaller Macs are untested, so report what actually ran. It needs Metal GPU access: if the worker log says `No Metal device available` (seen inside one coding agent's command sandbox), rerun outside the sandbox with a fresh `--out`; a failed job is never relaunched. One model at a time. Try at most two treatments in separate output directories.
3. Match NYC/Tiny London/SF: thin local-colour outlines, flat coherent shading, readable streets and source-supported roof differences. No clay. Compare real reference photos, native source and art for recognisable landmark silhouettes, measured scale, invented buildings, roofs and lost courtyards. A matching source/art pair can share the same wrong geometry. Save SHA-bound findings. Model completion is not geographic acceptance. Show the pilot beside its source and record the visual checks. Expand once they pass, unless the user requests an approval checkpoint.
4. Expand the accepted treatment with `atlas.py paint`; both source sides must reach 1024 pixels. Neighbours guide each next window; this is context infill, not joint denoising. Inspect overlap bands, landmarks and source-open parks for invented buildings. Open water invites invented islands: protect it with `paint --keep`. Keep failed studies outside Git. `atlas.py finish` replays reviewed colour masks or bounded native repairs with source, prior-pixel and asset hashes. Never reuse another city's masks or bypass a hash guard.
5. Export with `atlas.py showcase`, `atlas.py film` and `atlas.py social`. Preserve attribution in the viewer, metadata and sidecars. Films have zero text by default, optional anchored callouts at most seven words. No title or HUD. README GIFs use native held crops. [Commands, resume and review](docs/workflow.md).

Run tests before handing back. Bundled DC/Edinburgh examples must export offline, sources/art must retain their exact native registration, and no inference may silently shrink references. Keep the code small, source recipes explicit and captures/weights/results under ignored `outputs/`. Report actual source/art limits; do not equate byte checks with visual approval.

# Isometric cities

Real neighbourhoods as isometric pixel-art maps, made on your Mac by you and a coding agent.

[![Washington DC](examples/readme/dc.gif)](examples/dc.png)

[![Edinburgh](examples/readme/edinburgh.gif)](examples/edinburgh.png)

[Watch DC](https://github.com/Statecraft-Labs/isometric-cities/releases/download/v0.4.2/washington-dc.mp4) · [Make your city](https://github.com/Statecraft-Labs/isometric-cities/releases/download/v0.4.2/make-your-city.mp4)

## Ask for your city

Give your coding agent this:

```text
Clone https://github.com/Statecraft-Labs/isometric-cities and follow its AGENTS.md.
Make an isometric map of [CITY/AREA]. Review one accurate patch, then expand it.
```

Your agent sources real data, reviews a styled patch, then grows the map and exports an explorer and a film. Rendering and inference run locally on Apple Silicon; 128 GB tested, about 9 GB of weights.

Quality depends on available data. `make "PLACE"` starts with untextured geometry; the agent improves it before painting. The bundled native painter repainted the whole Edinburgh example from a fresh clone: 10 windows in 24 minutes, 18 GB at peak. A fresh coding agent given this README also used it to make a new Amsterdam map, from source capture to finished explorer and film, in about an hour with the models already downloaded. Smaller Macs are untested. [Method and limits](docs/workflow.md).

## Explore the examples

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Statecraft-Labs/isometric-cities.git
cd isometric-cities && ./setup.sh && python3 atlas.py demo --open
```

No models needed. Drag, pinch, jump between landmarks, compare each map with its source.

[Agent guide](AGENTS.md) · [Workflow](docs/workflow.md) · [Sources](docs/sources.md) · [How the examples were made](examples/README.md)

Code is MIT. The default Klein 9B weights are non-commercial. Maps and data keep [their own licences](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

# Source credits

The MIT licence covers this repository's original code. Source datasets, model weights and third-party libraries retain their own licences.

Maps use © OpenStreetMap contributors, [ODbL 1.0](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright). Acquired geometry and exported footprint databases retain source and licence records. Credits are included in each map manifest, website and film's associated description.

The Edinburgh recipe uses Scottish phase 5 LiDAR under [OGL v3](https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/). Credit: DTM: Crown copyright Scottish Government and Fugro (2021). DSM: Crown copyright Scottish Government and Fugro (2020).

The default Capitol Hill, Washington DC photographic recipe uses [DC 2023 aerial imagery](https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/aerial-photography-orthophoto-2023), CC BY 4.0; [2024 terrain](https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/2024-lidar-hydro-enforced-digital-terrain-model), CC0; and the older DC Office of Planning / CyberCity 3D building layer. Keep the District of Columbia Office of Planning credit with its geometry. OSM supplies footprint references and explicit dome parts. See [the source method](docs/sources.md).

The city examples retain source credits in `examples/dc.json` and `examples/edinburgh.json`. Edinburgh's geometry is Scottish LiDAR, not a composited photograph. Its material palette was informed by [Scotland-2016-Aerial-Edinburgh Castle](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Scotland-2016-Aerial-Edinburgh_Castle.jpg), Andrew Shiva / Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0. Edinburgh imagery and the derivative pipeline diagram are distributed under CC BY-SA 4.0. DC imagery retains CC BY 4.0 attribution.

The style uses [FLUX.2 Klein 9B q4](https://huggingface.co/mflux-community/flux2-klein-9b-mflux-q4), FLUX Non-Commercial, with [Pixel Art Redmond](https://huggingface.co/artificialguybr/PIXELART-REDMOND-FLUXKLEIN9B), Apache-2.0. Exact revisions and the adapter SHA are in `model-presets/pixelart-redmond-klein9b.json`. Model terms remain separate from source-image and code licences. No weights are bundled.

The portable coarse terrain option uses [Mapzen Skadi](https://github.com/tilezen/joerd/blob/master/docs/attribution.md), with underlying USGS, Copernicus and Environment Agency source credits recorded in the manifest. It is a mixed-source surface, not a surveyed building model.

Local image models are optional and downloaded separately. Record the model repository, exact revision and licence in each experiment. This code licence does not relicense those weights. No third-party style-reference image or model weight is bundled.

The local generation experiments were informed by the authors' primary writeups: [Isometric NYC](https://cannoneyed.com/projects/isometric-nyc), [Tiny London](https://tiny.london/how/), [Isometric SF](https://www.justinchavez.com/blog/isometric-sf/) and [Isometric Toronto](https://iso.sloptoronto.ca/how). This repository does not redistribute their maps or trained weights.

# Registered sources

Every source uses one camera and pixel lattice for the whole neighbourhood. Imagery colours surfaces in world coordinates before that camera projects them. Rotating a flat satellite photo cannot reveal facades.

## Washington DC

```sh
python3 atlas.py photo --city capitol-hill-dc --out outputs/dc-source
# Reuse that output's captured inputs, with network disabled:
python3 atlas.py photo --city capitol-hill-dc --out outputs/dc-source --offline
```

The default 8192×4096 capture uses 2.5 px/m and 35.264° equal-axis isometric elevation. It includes the White House, Eisenhower Executive Office Building, Washington Monument, National Mall museums, Capitol, Supreme Court, Library of Congress and Botanic Garden. Union Station is clipped at the top; the Jefferson Memorial is outside this frame.

The recipe configures ArcGIS ImageServer aerial/DTM rasters and the documented uncompressed I3S 1.6 building-mesh schema. Native raster chunks align exactly across provider download limits. ImageServer captures also count underlying catalogue rasters and subdivide requests to respect mosaic limits. A successful HTTP response alone does not establish coverage; offline replay requires the captured coverage receipt and matching raster hash. Roofs and ground sample aerial colour by world XY. Vertical walls use illustrative neutral materials and windows, never overhead pixels stretched down a facade. OSM supplies footprint references and explicit Capitol dome parts.

Sources: [DC 2023 aerial](https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/aerial-photography-orthophoto-2023), CC BY 4.0, 8 cm native sampled at 50 cm; [2024 DTM](https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/2024-lidar-hydro-enforced-digital-terrain-model), CC0, NAVD88 metres at 1 m; [DC Office of Planning / CyberCity 3D buildings](https://services.arcgis.com/neT9SoYxizqTHZPH/arcgis/rest/services/DC_3D_Buildings/SceneServer); and [OSM](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright), ODbL.

The legacy mesh predates the aerial and terrain. This is a historical mixture, including July 2026 OSM, and does not reconstruct 2025-2026 White House changes. Ornamentation and facade relief are approximate. The government-area DSM is redacted, so photography supplies vegetation appearance without measured current tree heights. Vertical residuals are recorded without guessing a geoid shift. Source-input hashes and assumptions stay in `manifest.json`.

Another city needs compatible licensed data and a new `photographic` recipe. This provider is not a universal photogrammetry downloader.

Optional `photographic.landmark_geometry` records add cited obelisks, arc colonnades and bounded facade corrections. Dimensions, materials, provider feature IDs and references live in the recipe. Invalid counts, coordinates, bands or missing provider features stop the render. These are illustrative source corrections, not surveyed ornament.

## Edinburgh

```sh
python3 atlas.py surface --city edinburgh --out outputs/edinburgh-source
python3 atlas.py surface --city edinburgh --out outputs/edinburgh-source --offline
```

The 3456×1803 source uses Scottish 0.5 m DSM/DTM at 3 px/m, looking northeast from the southwest at 30° elevation. This traditional 2:1 game view is technically dimetric. It includes Castle Rock, Old Town, Princes Street Gardens, Scott Monument, Waverley, Greyfriars, the museum and the Old College/McEwan Hall cluster. Holyrood is outside the frame.

The renderer range-reads configured public COG rasters, captures dated OSM geometry and downloads a SHA-pinned OSTN15 horizontal transformation grid. Preserve `outputs/cache/surface/edinburgh-v3/` for exact source replay. A fresh provider response creates newly recorded inputs; it need not match the delivered snapshot.

Measured roofs, chimneys, spires, terrain and tree canopy form one z-buffered surface. LiDAR contains no RGB. Tagged roof/wall materials take priority; untagged surfaces use slope and documented palette defaults. This does not reconstruct each roof's true colour. A 3×3 median smooths roof noise and can also shorten narrow features: on 0.5 m AHN it lowered the apex cell of Amsterdam's Nieuwe Kerk spire from 58.1 m to 49.4 m. Check a narrow landmark against the raw DSM. The palette is source-informed, not randomly varied. Another city can supply `surface.palette`.

Existing inputs can be supplied with `--surface PATH.npz --osm PATH.json --grid PATH.tif --offline`. NPZ contains finite `dsm`, `dtm` arrays of identical shape and `[west,south,east,north]` bounds, rows north to south. The recipe declares projected CRS and resolution. OSM must be Overpass `out body geom` JSON. `source.json` records all hashes, camera matrix, palette and landmarks.

For another location, a `surface` recipe supplies aligned DSM/DTM COG URLs, CRS, bounds, resolution, projected camera centre, bearing, elevation and screen bounds. Source data remains Scottish Crown copyright/Fugro under OGL v3 and OSM ODbL. [Full notices](../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

An optional `surface.landmarks` file can replace smeared heightfield buildings with footprint meshes, measured roof planes and authored landmark structures. The file binds the input hashes, CRS and exact camera; changed inputs require remeasurement. Edinburgh's example is under `cities/landmarks/`. Fine architectural details remain illustrative. Other cities can omit this layer or have their agent author a source-bound one.

For the bundled examples, use their source PNGs for styling without reacquiring data. Fresh Edinburgh provider responses can differ from the pinned landmark inputs and require the agent to remeasure that layer. The bundled source preserves the exact pixels used by the example.

## Any other neighbourhood

`atlas.py make "LOCATION"` produces a bounded OSM/Skadi starter when no photographic/surface recipe exists. It preserves source footprint holes, reconciles building parts, records numeric versus inferred heights, uses roof material/colour tags and declares untextured facades and terrain gaps. Missing terrain falls back explicitly. The starter is a place to inspect and improve, not photographic coverage or finished art.

Keep the exact source PNG, immutable source metadata and captured inputs. The bundled PNGs preserve the pixels used for each example even if a provider changes. Source geometry checks and an attractive model output are separate evidence; inspect landmarks and ordinary blocks before accepting either.

# Make a place

Apple Silicon macOS. `./setup.sh` installs source/export dependencies. Add `--models` to install a separate Python 3.12 MFlux runtime under `outputs/image-runtime` and download the pinned model and adapter, about 9 GB, public and ungated. Weights remain in the Hugging Face cache. The tested image environment, including transitive dependencies, is pinned in `source/image-requirements.txt`. FFmpeg is required for films and GIFs. Node is optional, used by the UI tests.

Development used one 128 GB Mac. A native 1024-pixel window peaked at 18.3 GB of MLX memory and took about two and a half minutes, model load included. Smaller machines are untested.

## Choose and inspect the source

```sh
python3 atlas.py make "Glasgow city centre"
```

Bundled aliases resolve first. "Capitol Hill" means Washington, DC. Any other place uses a cached Nominatim search, then a bounded OSM/Skadi starter. Explicit `"55.8609,-4.2514"` resolves offline. Sources record terrain gaps, tagged versus inferred heights, courtyard holes, camera and credits. Unknown places do not acquire photographic coverage automatically.

The starter is an untextured block model, 1024×640, small enough to style as one image. For a larger map, copy the generated `recipe.json`, add `"frame": {"padding_metres": 400}` under `camera` (2560×1600 at the default scale), and run `make` on that file with a new `--out`. `paint` needs both sides to reach 1024 pixels.

Use `--plan-only` to resolve without downloading/rendering sources or invoking a model. Source caches and receipts live under ignored `outputs/`. Repeat the same command to resume. `--offline` prohibits acquisition and needs cached inputs.

Improve the source before styling. Find primary licensed aerial, oblique, DSM or mesh data. Roof colour comes from tagged materials or registered imagery, never random variation. [Provider formats and examples](sources.md).

A supplied image can start a pilot immediately:

```sh
python3 atlas.py make "My location" --source /absolute/source.png \
  --manifest /absolute/source.json --crop 64 112 1024 1024 \
  --out outputs/my-pilot --plan-only
```

Crop values are literal X Y WIDTH HEIGHT. Inputs must be native RGB with no pending EXIF orientation. No resizing or out-of-bounds shifting occurs. A manifest binds the original image hash and camera; cropping translates only its matrix offsets. Omit it for an explicitly unregistered image study.

The full source remains intact up to 64 MP. The selected preset styles native 1024-square windows. Larger or unaligned images stay source-ready until you choose an exact crop or use `paint`.

Reuse a bundled source directly, without downloads:

```sh
python3 atlas.py make Edinburgh --source examples/edinburgh-source.png \
  --manifest examples/edinburgh.json --crop 240 779 1024 1024 --out outputs/castle
```

The supplied source is already registered. Acquiring a fresh Edinburgh surface can change the source hashes and needs remeasuring the optional landmark layer.

## Try one treatment

Repeat the pilot command with `--style --wait`. Use `--caption-file PATH` for visible materials and `--preset PATH` for another pinned model. The default is distilled Klein 9B q4 with Pixel Art Redmond at 0.7, four steps, CFG 1 and seed 4601. Name dominant materials only. Naming a rare material globally can spread it onto other roofs. Keep landmark names out of the `paint` caption too: every window reads it, and in one Amsterdam run a palace's courtyards spread onto ordinary canal blocks.

Styling runs in a fresh isolated MFlux worker using the downloaded pins. It runs offline, verifies native conditioning dimensions before inference, and serializes GPU workers. It never changes installed model code. There is no cloud fallback. It needs Metal GPU access. If `native-worker.log` reports `No Metal device available`, as it did inside one coding agent's command sandbox, move to a shell with GPU access. The failed job is kept and never relaunched, so give a pilot a fresh `--out`; for `paint`, use the failed-window recovery below.

The example maps were made differently: through `imagine`, a private local job queue running the same pinned model, adapter and settings. A compatible queue client is still used when `ATLAS_IMAGINE` names one or one is installed, and the worker then stands down so only one model loads. An unrelated program that merely shares the name is ignored. The native worker has repainted the full Edinburgh example from a fresh clone on the stock pinned runtime: 10 windows in 24 minutes. The result has the same style and layout as the queue's paint, with small differences in detail. It is not byte-identical, so the bundled finishing recipe refuses it, as its hash guard should. DC through the worker is untested.

Receipts advance through resolved, source-ready, queued, art-ready and reviewed. `--wait` checks an existing job for up to 45 seconds. Repeat to resume. Interrupted submissions recover their ID from the saved log; ambiguous submissions require inspecting that log and never submit twice automatically. A native worker that exits without a result is reported as failed at once. Changed recipes, source pixels, model settings and captions require a fresh `--out`.

Open the generated `viewer.html` directly. Inspect a landmark, an ordinary street and a park at native size. Compare colours, buildings, courtyards, light and outlines against the source. Model completion does not establish geographic acceptance. To record a review, add `--review PATH`. The JSON needs reviewer, decision, source_sha256, image_sha256, findings and four checks: landmarks, materials, geometry, native_detail. Acceptance requires all four to be `pass`; `reject` preserves the study.

## Expand the same treatment

```sh
python3 atlas.py paint --source examples/dc-source.png \
  --caption-file examples/dc-caption.txt --out outputs/dc-art
```

Substitute `edinburgh` for the other example. `--plan-only` reports the window count without resolving models or submitting work. Native 1024-square windows have at most an 800 px stride. Each next input includes finished neighbours, and a 128 px distance feather composes overlaps. This is sequential context infill, not shared-latent denoising. Cut display tiles only after the complete raster passes visual review.

Where a window holds nothing to redraw, the model invents: a window of open sea came back as an island of buildings. `--keep MASK.png` takes an 8-bit greyscale mask at the source size. White pixels keep the source and are never redrawn, and an all-white window gets no job. Draw the kept area into the source first, for example as flat water tones.

Every window keeps its input, raw prediction, settings and durable job receipt. Resume binds the source, prompt, preset, composition code and backend. A failed/ambiguous job is never replaced automatically. After reading its log, move that one folder out of `windows/` and repeat `paint`: finished windows are verified and reused, and only the missing one is submitted. `--adopt DIRECTORY` can replay original experimental windows, validating their exact neighbour context and pinned commands before composition.

The bundled recipes bind the original raw prediction hashes. Those raw paints are too large to bundle, so the `finish` command below reproduces the examples only from them. Re-inference can differ across Metal/runtime versions. If the fresh raw hash differs, review it and make a new finishing recipe. Do not disable a hash guard to reuse old masks.

```sh
python3 atlas.py finish --image outputs/dc-art/map.png \
  --source examples/dc-source.png --recipe examples/dc-finish.json \
  --out outputs/dc-finished
```

The finish preserves the native pixel grid. DC repairs source-open Monument lawn and the White House North Lawn fountain. Edinburgh applies its base-paint ink/material finish, then replaces the wrong Scott Monument using corrected measured source geometry and a calibrated local Gothic asset, and restores the St Giles crown finial. Source revisions and illustrative detail are recorded explicitly. Reviewed replacement PNGs, native support runs and hashes are bundled. `patches` run before material finishing; `post_patches` run after it and bind the finished prior pixels, so their accepted colours remain exact. Native scanline masks protect vegetation, neighbouring walls and unrelated landmarks. Each recipe binds raw/source hashes and records changed-pixel counts. Another city needs its own reviewed masks or repair asset.

## Explore and film

```sh
python3 atlas.py demo --open
python3 atlas.py showcase --image examples/dc.png \
  --source examples/dc-source.png --metadata examples/dc.json --out outputs/my-viewer
python3 atlas.py film --image examples/dc.png --manifest examples/dc.json \
  --output outputs/dc-flythrough.mp4 --seconds 60 --fps 60 --width 1920 --height 1080
```

A `make` source's `capture/source.json` works as `--metadata` and `--manifest` as it is. A `surface` source records its landmarks by name instead, so give `showcase` a small file like `examples/dc.json`: `landmarks` as a list of `id`, `name`, `x`, `y` in native pixels, plus `credits`.

The offline explorer loads only the visible tiles, with small previews for instant navigation. Drag to pan, pinch or scroll to zoom, and use the divider to compare source and art in the same viewport. The places menu jumps directly to named landmarks. Phone controls have 44-pixel tap targets; Scott Monument and the White House open at native scale. Number keys also hop to landmarks; any input stops the tour. The minimap supports click and drag. Credits remain in the viewer, and reduced motion disables automatic movement. Deep Zoom lower levels use box filtering; native tiles reconstruct the map exactly. Default `demo` selects an immutable edition under `outputs/demo/`, so updated examples open correctly while old exports survive. An explicit `--out` stays strict: use a fresh directory when inputs change.

For iPhone Safari on the same Wi-Fi, run `python3 atlas.py demo --serve --host 0.0.0.0`. Open `http://YOUR-MAC-LAN-ADDRESS:8765/` on the phone. Only the current exported map folder is served, and Ctrl-C stops it. The default `--serve` host is loopback; no site is deployed. A real iOS Safari device still needs its own acceptance check.

The supplied film routes use 1:1 pixels, with no title, HUD or callouts. Credits travel in MP4 metadata and `.credits.txt`; retain them in a sharing description. Optional `--callouts` allows at most seven on-screen words. Its leader tips use original map anchors, independent of camera clamping. The exporter checks every planned viewport and writes route/bounds sidecars. Before sharing, inspect encoded frames and fully decode the movie: `ffmpeg -v error -xerror -i outputs/dc-flythrough.mp4 -f null -`.

```sh
python3 atlas.py social --manifest examples/dc.json --output outputs/dc-social.mp4
```

`social` cuts a 1080×1350 portrait film for a phone feed: keyed shots, no text, and a last frame that returns to the first so it loops. A shot list lives beside the manifest as `NAME-social.json`. The DC list opens on finished art of the Capitol, cuts to the Washington Monument and the White House, then sweeps the registered source into art at three seconds. Without a list, the manifest landmarks make a default that opens split between source and art and wipes to art. Each shot has `seconds`, a `path` of keys (`at` a landmark ID or map X,Y, optional `offset` and `width` in map pixels) and optional `ease` and `wipe`. Shots cut unless neighbours share a key. Views stay within 1.25× of native unless the recipe sets `pixel_zoom`; closer views square the pixels, never smooth them. `--plan-only` checks every frame and writes the poster and a phone-sized contact sheet. Inspect those before encoding. The portrait master is retained at full quality. For a smaller 720×900 upload copy with a silent AAC track:

```sh
ffmpeg -i outputs/dc-social.mp4 -f lavfi -i anullsrc=r=48000:cl=stereo \
  -map 0:v:0 -map 1:a:0 -map_metadata 0 -vf scale=720:900:flags=lanczos \
  -c:v libx264 -crf 18 -c:a aac -shortest -movflags +faststart outputs/dc-x.mp4
```

```sh
python3 atlas.py tease --image examples/dc.png --manifest examples/dc.json \
  --output outputs/dc.gif --centres 6650,1110 886,2670 2688,3335 4300,2530
```

README GIFs hold four native 800×450 crops for two seconds each. No overlays or interpolation. Edinburgh centres are `760,1330 1850,660 860,470 1450,390`. Static fallbacks are the first native crops.

## Change a recipe

Add one JSON file under `cities/`, or give `make` its path. The recipe owns aliases, origin, bounds, landmarks and provider/camera settings. The two bundled recipes show each provider. Copy a generated recipe outside its run before editing, then use a new output directory. For high-altitude places, terrain establishes camera focus; a measured `landmarks[0].elevation_m` can override it. Explicit screen/elevation bounds require your own coverage check.

Nominatim lookups are cached and serialized at one request per second, with attribution and an identifying user agent. No autocomplete or bulk searching. Set `ATLAS_GEOCODER_URL` for another compatible endpoint. Cached failures require inspection before deliberate retry. Geocoding establishes a centre, not imagery coverage.

Run `python3 atlas.py doctor`, `.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, and optionally `ruff check atlas.py source tests --select F`. Keep weights, captures, failures and private coordinates out of commits. New scenes need their own source and art review.

# Separate neighbourhoods

[DC map](dc.png) · [Edinburgh map](edinburgh.png) · [Pipeline](pipeline.png)

DC covers the White House, Washington Monument, National Mall museums, Capitol, Library of Congress, Supreme Court, Senate and House offices, Botanic Garden and American Indian museum. Edinburgh covers the Castle and Rock, Royal Mile, St Giles, Princes Street, Waverley, Greyfriars, National Museum, Old College, McEwan Hall and Teviot. Holyrood and the Jefferson Memorial are outside these frames; Union Station is clipped.

Each city has its own native source, art PNG, caption, finishing recipe and JSON provenance. `dc.json` and `edinburgh.json` bind the actual file hashes, camera, local model, window composition and geographic limitations. Sources and art have identical dimensions. The map is completed before display tiles are cut.

## What was actually done

Real 3D sources → one fixed camera per city → native 1024-square edits with a public pixel-art LoRA → completed neighbours included in each next input → 128 px overlap feather → bounded local colour finish → explorer and silent film.

All image inference ran on one Mac through `imagine`, a private local job queue, using Klein 9B q4, four steps, guidance 1, Redmond scale 0.7 and seeds starting at 4601. The map-generation method is **context infill, not shared-latent sampling**. There is no local training or cloud image teacher in this recipe.

DC includes bounded repairs for invented buildings on the Monument lawn and a tree that replaced the White House North Lawn fountain. Edinburgh gets a gentle outline lift and Great Hall slate tint. Its Scott Monument was rebuilt from the real mapped footprint and measured height, then given a local Gothic art asset calibrated to that corrected silhouette. Its four outer turrets stand free of the arched base, as in the source. St Giles keeps its source-height crown finial. Fine tracery and the statue are illustrative. Replacement PNGs, source/prior-pixel hashes and native support runs are bundled. Exact finishing replay also needs the original raw paints, which are not. The base-paint source hash remains recorded separately from the corrected source. Some facade patterns and tiny ornaments are invented. See each JSON's limitations and compare the source in the viewer.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
repo_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
if [[ $# -gt 1 || ( $# -eq 1 && "$1" != --models ) ]]; then
  echo 'Usage: ./setup.sh [--models]'; exit 1
fi
if ! command -v uv >/dev/null; then
  if command -v brew >/dev/null; then brew install uv
  else echo 'Install uv from https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/ then run ./setup.sh'; exit 1; fi
fi
if command -v brew >/dev/null && ! command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null; then brew install ffmpeg; fi
if [[ ! -x "$repo_dir/.venv/bin/python" ]]; then uv venv --python 3.13 "$repo_dir/.venv"; fi
uv pip install --python "$repo_dir/.venv/bin/python" -r "$repo_dir/source/requirements.txt"
if [[ "${1:-}" == --models ]]; then
  if [[ "$(uname -s)" != Darwin || "$(uname -m)" != arm64 ]]; then
    echo 'Local image inference needs Apple Silicon macOS.'; exit 1
  fi
  image_env="$repo_dir/outputs/image-runtime"
  if [[ ! -x "$image_env/bin/python" ]]; then uv venv --python 3.12 "$image_env"; fi
  uv pip install --python "$image_env/bin/python" -r "$repo_dir/source/image-requirements.txt"
  echo 'Fetching the pinned model and adapter into the Hugging Face cache (about 9 GB on first run).'
  "$image_env/bin/python" - "$repo_dir" <<'PY'
import json,sys
from pathlib import Path
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download,hf_hub_download
root=Path(sys.argv[1]);preset=json.loads((root/'model-presets/pixelart-redmond-klein9b.json').read_text())
base,adapter=preset['base'],preset['adapter']
snapshot_download(base['repo'],revision=base['revision'])
hf_hub_download(adapter['repo'],adapter['filename'],revision=adapter['revision'])
sys.path.insert(0,str(root/'source'))
from local_style import model_paths
print('Pinned model and adapter ready:',model_paths(preset))
PY
fi
# A missing FFmpeg only stops films and GIFs. The demo runs without it, so setup still succeeds.
"$repo_dir/.venv/bin/python" "$repo_dir/atlas.py" doctor || true

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Cache OSM geometry and every Skadi degree tile required by a city config."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import shutil
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import requests

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
from geometry import hgt_tiles
from project import digest, recipe_path, read

ENDPOINTS = ['https://overpass.openstreetmap.fr/api/interpreter','https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter','https://overpass.private.coffee/api/interpreter','https://overpass.kumi.systems/api/interpreter']
DEM_ATTRIBUTION = 'Mapzen Terrain Tiles. USGS SRTM/GMTED2010, Copernicus EU-DEM, UK © Environment Agency 2015; exact per-pixel source not identified.'


def fetch(city, refresh=False, offline=False):
    folder=Path(city['data_dir'])
    folder.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    session=requests.Session()
    session.headers['User-Agent']='PortableIsometricCity/0.2 (OSM geometry renderer)'
    bbox=','.join(str(v) for v in city['bbox'])
    query=f'''[out:json][timeout:180][bbox:{bbox}];
    (nwr[building];nwr["building:part"];way[highway];relation[highway];way[railway];
     nwr[leisure];nwr[landuse];nwr[natural];nwr[water];way[waterway];
     way[barrier];nwr[historic];nwr[tourism=attraction];);out body geom;'''
    query_path=folder/'overpass-query.txt'
    meta_path=folder/'provenance.json'
    old=json.loads(meta_path.read_text()) if meta_path.exists() else {}
    osm=folder/'osm.json'
    if osm.exists() and not refresh and old.get('bbox_south_west_north_east') not in (None,city['bbox']):
        raise ValueError('OSM cache belongs to different bounds; use a fresh cache or refresh explicitly')
    if not refresh:
        for name,record in old.get('files',{}).items():
            cached=folder/name
            if not cached.is_file() or digest(cached)!=record['sha256']:
                raise ValueError(f'Cached source input changed: {cached}. Use a fresh cache or refresh explicitly')
    imported=None
    if not osm.exists() and city.get('osm_source') and not refresh:
        original=Path(city['osm_source']).expanduser()
        if not original.is_absolute(): original=ROOT/original
        if original.exists():
            shutil.copy2(original,osm)
            imported=str(original)
            original_meta=original.parent/'provenance.json'
            if original_meta.exists():
                old=json.loads(original_meta.read_text())
    endpoint=old.get('osm_endpoint')
    retrieved=old.get('retrieved_at')
    if refresh or not osm.exists():
        if offline:
            raise RuntimeError(f'Offline mode requires an OSM cache: {osm}')
        for candidate in ENDPOINTS:
            try:
                print(f'Fetching OSM from {candidate}',flush=True)
                response=session.get(candidate,params={'data':query},timeout=200)
                response.raise_for_status()
                payload=response.json()
                if payload.get('remark') or not payload.get('elements'):
                    raise RuntimeError(payload.get('remark','Empty Overpass result'))
                osm.write_text(json.dumps(payload,separators=(',',':')))
                query_path.write_text(query+'\n')
                endpoint=candidate
                retrieved=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
                break
            except (requests.RequestException,ValueError,RuntimeError) as error:
                print(f'OSM endpoint failed: {error}',flush=True)
        else:
            raise RuntimeError('No Overpass endpoint returned a complete result')
        reused_osm=False
    else:
        reused_osm=True
    spec=city['terrain']
    need_skadi=spec['provider']=='skadi' or spec['provider']=='lidar' and spec.get('fallback','skadi')=='skadi'
    sources={Path(p).name:(Path(p) if Path(p).is_absolute() else ROOT/p) for p in city.get('dem_sources',[])}
    dem_records=[]
    for tile in hgt_tiles(city['bbox']) if need_skadi else []:
        path=folder/f'{tile}.hgt.gz'
        url=f'https://s3.amazonaws.com/elevation-tiles-prod/skadi/{tile[:3]}/{tile}.hgt.gz'
        if not path.exists() and path.name in sources and not refresh:
            shutil.copy2(sources[path.name],path)
        error=None
        if (refresh or not path.exists()) and not offline:
            try:
                print(f'Fetching DEM from {url}',flush=True)
                response=session.get(url,timeout=90)
                response.raise_for_status()
                path.write_bytes(response.content)
            except requests.RequestException as failure:
                error=str(failure)
                print(f'DEM unavailable; manifest will record flat/missing terrain: {failure}',flush=True)
        dem_records.append({'tile':tile,'url':url,'cached':path.exists(),'error':error})
    header=json.loads(osm.read_text())
    files=[osm]+[folder/f"{r['tile']}.hgt.gz" for r in dem_records if r['cached']]
    # A cache can contain documented supplemental geometry. Keep its acquisition
    # evidence when reusing it; a fresh base download invalidates that evidence.
